banner: Free AI that decides, not writes

yt.title: An AI that can't write
notes: It never writes text; it answers fixed questions
32,138 GitHub stars in 3 weeks (as of Oct 10)
What it's good at, and what its own page admits

lines.text: This free AI can't write a single sentence. [1] Yet thirty-two thousand developers starred it in three weeks. [2] Here's what it's good at, and what its own page admits.

yt.title: Fixed questions, one number
notes: Laya, by Nandakishor (Kerala)
Example: 1,000 refund emails a day
It answers a fixed question, no reply written
Real output: 94% sure (base model, run by us)

lines.text: It's Laya, by Nandakishor from Kerala. [1] Picture a thousand emails a day like 'We were billed twice, please refund.' [2] Laya doesn't write replies. It answers a fixed question: is this a refund request? [3] We ran it: ninety-four percent sure.
lines.show: It's Laya, by Nandakishor from Kerala. [1] Picture 1,000 emails a day like 'We were billed twice, please refund.' [2] Laya doesn't write replies. It answers a fixed question: is this a refund request? [3] We ran it: 94% sure.
lines.tts: It's Laa-ya, by Nanda-kishore, from Kerala. Picture a thousand emails a day, like: we were billed twice, please refund. Laa-ya doesn't write replies. It answers a fixed question: is this a refund request? We ran it: ninety four percent sure.

yt.title: Fast, free, no rambling
notes: ~33 ms a question on a cloud GPU (his page)
Free, open source (Apache-2.0)
It can be wrong, but it can't ramble

lines.text: Why use it? [1] It's fast: about thirty-three milliseconds a question on a cloud GPU. [2] It's free and open source. [3] And since it never writes, it can be wrong, but it can't ramble.
lines.show: Why use it? [1] It's fast: about 33 milliseconds a question on a cloud GPU. [2] It's free and open source. [3] And since it never writes, it can be wrong, but it can't ramble.
lines.tts: Why use it? It's fast: about thirty three milliseconds a question, on a cloud G P U. It's free, and open source. And since it never writes, it can be wrong, but it can't ramble.

yt.title: From his own page
notes: Great on what it was trained on (spam 99%)
New business tasks: 36% out of the box vs 46% for always guessing the most common answer; 77% after training (his reported number)
20+ options: Jev (paid) does better
Telugu: 22% on a 20-option test (English 71%)

lines.text: The catch, from his own page: [1] it's great at what it was trained on, like spam, but on new business tasks it's worse than guessing the most common answer, until you train it on your examples. [2] With many options, the paid rival Jev does better. [3] And in Telugu, it gets about one in five right.
lines.show: The catch, from his own page: [1] it's great at what it was trained on, like spam, but on new business tasks it's worse than guessing the most common answer, until you train it on your examples. [2] With many options, the paid rival Jev does better. [3] And in Telugu, it gets about one in five right.
lines.tts: The catch, from his own page. It's great at what it was trained on, like spam. But on new business tasks, it's worse than guessing the most common answer, until you train it, on your own examples. With many options, the paid rival, Jevv, does better. And in Telugu, it gets about one in five right.

Telugu: not yet
